claim: Fourteenth Army planned for about 25,000 prisoners; about 75,000 American and Filipino troops surrendered on 9 April 1942
source: Wikipedia, Battle of Bataan (citing PBS The War and Britannica); HistoryNet, 'Was the Bataan Death March War Crimes Trial Fair?'
note: Secondary sources only; Japanese staff records not opened.

claim: About 350 to 400 Filipino officers and NCOs were executed at the Pantingan River on Tsuji's initiative; Homma was convicted by the Manila tribunal and executed in April 1946
note: Sources differ on numbers and nationality of victims.

claim: About 27 percent of Western prisoners held by Japan died, against about 4 percent in German and Italian hands
source: Wikipedia, Prisoners of war in World War II

claim: Japanese records give some 87 civilians killed; other accounts give about 50. Cities bombed: Tokyo, Yokohama, Yokosuka, Nagoya, Kobe, Osaka
source: HistoryNet, 'Aftermath of the Doolittle Raid Reexamined'; Wikipedia, Doolittle Raid

claim: Eight airmen captured, three shot on 15 October 1942, five commuted, one died in captivity; Zhejiang and Jiangxi reprisal campaign
Parshall and Tully (Shattered Sword) reject the 'five fatal minutes' account
source: HistoryNet and StrategyPage reviews of Shattered Sword
note: The game no longer cites them; the earlier text said the opposite. Confirm in the book before citing.

claim: Ribbentrop to Ott, 10 July 1941: Germany and Japan should join hands on the trans-Siberian railroad before winter
note: Paraphrased in the game, no quotation marks.

claim: Japanese casualties at Imphal about 55,000 (54,879 killed and wounded)
note: Estimates of the dead alone run to about 30,000.

claim: Marshall revived a limited proposal for gas against bypassed cave positions in May 1945; Truman refused it in June on Roosevelt's no-first-use policy; a Chemical Warfare Service study of June 1945 considered gas in the invasion
source: USNI Proceedings, 'The Most Deadly Plan' (1998); USNI Naval History, 'Another Alternative: Poison Gas' (2015); National WWII Museum, 'The Horribles'
note: The Kagoshima detail and a Stilwell memorandum could not be confirmed and were removed.

claim: Compton sat on the Scientific Panel that recommended military use without demonstration; he did not sign the Franck Report (chaired by James Franck)
source: Standard histories of the Interim Committee
note: The dossier and the adviser were wrong and were corrected.

claim: Lockwood's net test in Australia in 1942 found the Mark 14 ran about ten feet deep; Bureau of Ordnance confirmed it in August 1942; the contact pin was fixed in September 1943
source: Standard histories of the submarine war (Blair, Silent Victory)

claim: Adams letter January 1942; Carlsbad airfield fire May 1943; cancelled 1944 after about two million dollars
note: The node was redated from January to May 1943.

claim: 320 killed, 202 of them Black enlisted men; 258 refused on 9 August; 50 convicted of mutiny
source: Standard accounts; National Park Service, Port Chicago Naval Magazine
note: Sentences and later clemency not stated in the text.
